note: main() parses the attacker-controlled command line with getopt_long(); a '--'-prefixed long option is dispatched to the compatibility getopt implementation.
The option text following '--' is captured as current_argv; this text comes from an argument buffer that is only length-tracked (current_argv_len) and is not guaranteed to be NUL-terminated.
The option text is scanned for '=' so that the option-name prefix length can be tracked separately.
Only current_argv_len (the length up to '=') is recorded; no NUL terminator is inserted at that boundary, so the buffer's true end is not known to the error-reporting code.
Long options are matched by prefix; an option name that matches no entry leaves match == -1.
No long option matches the supplied text, so the unknown-option error-reporting branch is taken.

Error reporting passes current_argv with the '%s'-style illoptstring format even though the option text is only bounded by current_argv_len and is not guaranteed to be NUL-terminated; fprintf will scan for a terminator that may lie past the end of the argument buffer.
Inside fprintf the '%s' conversion reads current_argv past the end of the non-NUL-terminated argument buffer, producing an out-of-bounds read.
